[LTIM.10.7] **Resolving a zone.** To resolve a designation `Z` other than
`"UTC"` ([LTIM.10.8]) at an instant `t`, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch,
the engine must take, among the live `TimeZoneOffset` facts ([LTIM.10.6]) whose
`zone` equals `Z` byte for byte, the one with the greatest `valid_from` not after
`t`. If that fact's `valid_until` is after `t`, its `offset_s` is the answer.
Otherwise, and when no such fact exists, `Z` has no answer at `t`
([LTIM.10.5.3]). The facts of one zone may overlap: this rule decides which one
answers, whatever order they arrived in.

A period is half-open, so no `valid_until` is after the last instant of the
`Time` range ([LTIM.1.1.5]), and no zone but `"UTC"` has an answer there: a
read in `Z` at that instant is [LTIM.10.5.3]'s failure, however the facts are
written. The longest period a fact can state ends one nanosecond before it.

A resolution must cost O(log r), where r is the number of live
`TimeZoneOffset` facts whose `zone` is `Z`, and must not depend on any other
fact ([LCNT.5.2]).

A resolution sees every `TimeZoneOffset` fact the host has asserted, replaced
or retracted before it. No host assert or retract runs during a pump
([NLFC.3.3], [RARC.13.16]), so every resolution of one zone at one instant within a pump
answers alike. A replay delivers those facts where the trace records them
([LFST.6.1.1]), so it resolves as the recorded run did.

A change to a zone's facts re-evaluates a `where` that resolves the zone, as
any time-dependent condition is re-evaluated ([LTIM.2.4.1], [LTIM.2.5.1]). It
does not re-run an action that has already fired: a value an action computed
from an earlier fact stands.
